description: Planted, uncommented violations across 6 fixtures — used to compare with_skill vs without_skill (or old vs new skill version) runs of onion-architecture. No fixture contains hints or comments revealing the issue; each maps to exactly one Core Principle in SKILL.md.

findings.description: Route handler does role-based visibility filtering (`items.filter(...)` on `user.role`) and unread filtering inline instead of delegating to a service — business logic living in the presentation layer.
`new NotificationsRepository(app.container.db)` instantiated directly inside the route handler instead of being pulled from `container`.

Service imports the Drizzle `labels` schema and runs `container.db.select().from(labels)` directly, bypassing `LabelsRepository` (which exists in the same fixture but is never used) — Drizzle query building leaking into the application layer.
`repository.ts` (infrastructure) imports `normalizeDeliveryStatus` from `service.ts` (application) — a backward, outward-pointing import. Infrastructure must never depend on application code.
`WebhooksRepository` instantiates `new ReposRepository(db)` itself in its constructor instead of receiving it via the container — a repository composing another repository outside `container.ts`.
`ExportsService` constructor does `new S3StorageAdapter(container.config.s3Bucket)` — adapter instantiated inside a service instead of in `container.ts`.
`import type { FastifyReply } from 'fastify'` in the application layer — a framework type leaking past the presentation layer into a service.

`process.env.RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` and `process.env.RATE_LIMIT_MAX` read directly inside the repository instead of via `container.config`. Deliberately planted to test the new Core Principle 7 rule in isolation — no `new ConcreteClass()` adapter-instantiation confound present in this fixture.

`summarizeRecent` loops over `ids` calling `findById` + `countRunsForPr` once per id (two single-item repository calls inside the loop) instead of adding batched `findByIds`/`countRunsForPrs` methods. Deliberately planted to test the new Core Principle 8 rule.
